source_event.finding: A-006 renewed temporal horizon emitted a milestone that predated the horizon

generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: When a finite deadline is extended, renewed or replanned, a scheduler can reuse the previous origin while recomputing markers from the new end, causing markers to appear before the new horizon exists or duplicate the activation boundary.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: The new deadline is correct and idempotency keys are stable, but reminder dates are derived only from the new end and are never filtered against the creation/start of the renewed horizon.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Treat every renewed finite deadline as a new temporal horizon: derive its actual start, reject or omit markers before that start, and coalesce a named marker that coincides with activation into one canonical event.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Start from a prior horizon, create a shorter renewed horizon, and test before activation, exactly at activation, a reachable later marker and retry; no event may predate the renewed horizon and activation may not duplicate an equivalent named marker.

transfer_cases.evidence: Synthetic 14-unit renewed window excludes a longer D30 marker and still emits D7 later.
